question: Should a slow `socket.drain` subscriber preserve the existing connection-safe shedding behavior and resynchronize, or be disconnected immediately when the teardown frame cannot be queued?
rationale: This is an externally observable Gateway compatibility and availability contract; the latest patch chooses disconnect-without-delivery, and implementation evidence cannot determine whether that policy is intended.

options.title: Preserve and resync
options.body: Keep existing slow-client safety and add deterministic snapshot or sequence reconciliation for any missed drain event.

options.title: Disconnect on drain
options.body: Keep the current close behavior, document it as the public contract, and prove downstream reconnect recovery under controlled pressure.

options.title: Defer the event
options.body: Pause the feature until maintainers agree on a reliable teardown-notification contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve and resync
recommendation.body: Keep existing slow-client safety and add deterministic snapshot or sequence reconciliation for any missed drain event.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history directly connects this routing candidate to both the session-change consolidation and slow-socket broadcaster behavior defining the decision.
